newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer sees no shift from steady rate policy.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer sees no shift from steady rate policy.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Sunday he saw no reason for the German central bank to deviate from its steady hand policy on interest rates.
"Steady hand monetary policy is something that I believe has paid off, which is correct, which is necessary," he said in an interview with German radio, a text of which was released in advance.
"And at the moment I see no reason to change this monetary policy," Tietmeyer added.
Tietmeyer also said that Germany was in a happy position of having an inflation rate well below two percent and hoped to keep it below that level in the longer term.

The Bundesbank has kept its headline Lombard and discount rates on hold since last April, when it eased them to 4.50 percent and 2.50 percent respectively. The money market rate, or repo, has been at three percent since August.
